preamble: Pharyngealization of the glottal stop [ʔ] to the voiced pharyngeal fricative [ʕ], the reverse of the far more common ʕ > ʔ. In Tigre, ʔ and ʕ vary freely in words that also contain an emphatic or a true pharyngeal, which McCarthy (1994) analyses as the pharyngeal feature spreading onto ʔ.

examples.note: Free variation conditioned by the emphatic q in the same word; the ʔ/ʕ contrast is neutralized in words with emphatics or true pharyngeals.
Conditioned by the pharyngeal ḥ in the same word.
Blin has /ʕ/ for Proto-Agaw initial *ʔ, which Awngi keeps as a glottal onset.

sources: McCarthy, J. J. (1994). The phonetics and phonology of Semitic pharyngeals. In P. Keating (Ed.), Papers in Laboratory Phonology III. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9780511659461.012
McCarthy, J. J. (1994). The phonetics and phonology of Semitic pharyngeals (author's manuscript). http://people.umass.edu/jjmccart/guttural.pdf
